sentences.en: The snow filled the air with a soft grey-blue mist, softening the wind and gunfire, bringing the earth and sky together into one swaying blur.
sentences.zh: 雪花在空气中弥漫，化作一层柔和的蓝灰色薄雾，减弱了风势和炮火，将天地融为一体，成了一片摇曳的朦胧。

sentences.en: The snow fell on Bach's shoulders.
sentences.zh: 雪落在巴赫的肩头。

sentences.en: It was as though flakes of silence were falling on the still vulgar, on the dead city, on the skeletons of horses.
sentences.zh: 仿佛一片片寂静，正落在依然粗俗的、死去的城市上，落在马的骨架上。

sentences.en: It was snowing everywhere, on earth and on the stars.
sentences.zh: 到处都在下雪，大地上，繁星间。

sentences.en: The whole universe was full of snow.
sentences.zh: 整个宇宙都积满了雪。

sentences.en: Everything was disappearing beneath it.
sentences.zh: 一切都在雪下消失。

sentences.en: Guns, the bodies of the dead, filthy dressings, rubble, scraps of twisted iron.
sentences.zh: 枪支、尸体、污秽的绷带、瓦砾、扭曲的铁片。

sentences.en: This soft white snow settling over the carnage of the city was time itself.
sentences.zh: 这层柔和的白雪覆盖在城市的血泊与废墟之上，它本身就是时间。

sentences.en: The present was turning into the past, and there was no future.
sentences.zh: 现在正在变成过去，而未来已不复存在。

sentences.en: Welcome to The Rest is History, and that was Vasily Grossman in his great novel Life and Fate,
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余烬》，刚才那是瓦西里·格罗斯曼在他伟大的小说《生存与命运》中的描写，

sentences.en: drawing on his experience as a war reporter during the Battle of Stalingrad in the last months of 1942.
sentences.zh: 取材于他1942年底斯大林格勒战役期间担任战地记者的亲身经历。

sentences.en: So, Tom, we ended the last episode with German and Soviet troops fighting house to house, and winter was coming over closer, and our guest Ian McGregor is still with us.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，我们在上一集的结尾讲到德国和苏联军队在进行逐屋争夺，冬天越来越近了，我们的嘉宾伊恩·麦格雷戈也依然和我们在一起。

sentences.en: And Ian, can we kick off by talking about one of the really iconic things about Stalingrad,
sentences.zh: 伊恩，我们能不能先聊聊斯大林格勒最具标志性的事物之一，

sentences.en: something I know you're really interested in, which is the story of Pavlov and his house.
sentences.zh: 我知道你对这个非常感兴趣，那就是巴甫洛夫和他的房子的故事。

sentences.en: Because your book is called The Lighthouse of Stalingrad, and I mean, obviously, it's a podcast,
sentences.zh: 因为你的书名叫《斯大林格勒的灯塔》，我的意思是，显然这是一个播客，

sentences.en: so people can't see the map, but if you can imagine, there is a square very close to the Volga River called the 9th of January Square, and it's flanked by all these buildings.
sentences.zh: 所以大家看不到地图，但如果你能想象一下，伏尔加河附近有一个广场叫一月九日广场，周围环绕着各种建筑。

sentences.en: The German forces have sort of got down to the square, and there's one building that sort of sticks out into the square, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 德军已经推进到了广场附近，有一栋建筑突出在广场上，对吧？

sentences.en: It's an apartment building, and this is the building that becomes famous, the famous building of Stalingrad called Pavlov's House.
sentences.zh: 那是一栋公寓楼，这就是那栋后来闻名遐迩的斯大林格勒著名建筑——巴甫洛夫的房子。

sentences.en: So, tell us about who Pavlov is and why his house matters.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲巴甫洛夫是谁，以及他的房子为什么重要。

sentences.en: Junior Sergeant Pavlov is a bit like Chukov.
sentences.zh: 准尉巴甫洛夫有点像崔可夫。

sentences.en: He was born in a village outside of Moscow, about 50 miles outside of Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他出生在莫斯科郊外的一个村庄，离莫斯科大约50英里。

sentences.en: He joined up at the start of the war,
sentences.zh: 他在战争初期应征入伍，

sentences.en: and he was in the elite formations because the guards' rifle divisions that had been created were seen as the elite of the Russian Red Army Armed Forces,
sentences.zh: 并且进入了精锐部队，因为当时组建的近卫步兵师被视为苏联红军武装力量的精锐，

sentences.en: better trained, better equipment, better pay, better food.
sentences.zh: 训练更好、装备更好、津贴更高、伙食更好。

sentences.en: And he was in Radimtsev's 13th Guards that had gone over on this suicidal, almost like Omaha Beach, assault onto the western shore
sentences.zh: 他属于罗季姆采夫的第13近卫师，该师曾进行过一场几乎如同奥马哈海滩登陆般九死一生的突击，强渡到西岸，

sentences.en: to reclaim the central part of the city which the Germans had taken the day before, and they did manage to drive them back.
sentences.zh: 以夺回前一天被德军占领的市中心，他们确实成功地把德军打了回去。

sentences.en: And what you have, therefore, going forward over the next few weeks and months is this brutal house-to-house fighting for just the few inches of ground,
sentences.zh: 因此，在接下来的几周和几个月里，接下来发生的就是为了区区几英寸土地、

sentences.en: a few feet of ground, the next room, the next floor.
sentences.zh: 几英尺土地、下一个房间、下一层楼而展开的残酷逐屋争夺战。

sentences.en: Hopefully, you capture the next building.
sentences.zh: 希望能攻占下一栋建筑。

sentences.en: The 9th of January Square is literally 600, 700 metres away from the Volga, and behind that is the central landing pier where the main supplies of troops
sentences.zh: 一月九日广场距离伏尔加河字面意义上只有600、700米远，其后方就是中央登陆码头，主要的主力部队

sentences.en: and ammunition, as well as the wounded going in the other direction, were.
sentences.zh: 和弹药，以及往相反方向运送伤员的转运站都在那里。

sentences.en: And that's where Radimtsev had his headquarters.
sentences.zh: 这也是罗季姆采夫设立指挥部的地方。

sentences.en: And it was up to him to have his three regiments along this line that would defend the pockets of resistance in the centre of the city.
sentences.zh: 他负责让麾下的三个团沿着这条防线，坚守市中心的各个抵抗据点。

sentences.en: And what evolved was it was the case of following Chukev's orders that there would be an active defence, which came all the way from Moscow.
sentences.zh: 随之演变出来的，是遵照崔可夫关于进行积极防御的命令，这一战术一直追溯到莫斯科。

sentences.en: Stalin wanted to see this.
sentences.zh: 斯大林希望看到这一点。

sentences.en: He wanted to let the Russian people know that they were fighting to defend the city and they were taking the fight to the Germans.
sentences.zh: 他要让俄罗斯人民知道，他们正在为保卫这座城市而战，而且他们在向德军主动发起进攻。

sentences.en: They weren't just passively waiting to be attacked.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是被动地等待挨打。

sentences.en: So this active defence spawned or evolved the doctrine of the storm troops.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种积极防御催生或演变出了突击队的战术。

sentences.en: Pavlov became part of this.
sentences.zh: 巴甫洛夫也成为了其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Instead of mass assaults by company-sized formations, which would then be decimated by German artillery, assault guns or aerial attacks,
sentences.zh: 不再是连级规模的集群冲锋，那样只会遭到德国火炮、突击炮或空袭的毁灭性打击，

sentences.en: they would shrink this down to six-man teaMs.
sentences.zh: 他们将部队缩减为六人小组。

sentences.en: Normally, six-man teams could be eight-man teaMs.
sentences.zh: 通常六人小组，也可能是八人小组。

sentences.en: And they would be armed to the teeth.
sentences.zh: 并且他们会武装到牙齿。

sentences.en: So they would have the latest submachine guns, like I was saying, their pocket artillery, which was bags of grenades.
sentences.zh: 他们会配备最新的冲锋枪，就像我说的，还有他们的袖珍火炮——一袋袋的手榴弹。

sentences.en: And it would be up to them to be the vanguard to see if they could take these buildings that were further into the heart of the city
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是充当先锋，看能否攻占那些更深入城市腹地的建筑，

sentences.en: that might be able to allow Radimsev to then push the line further away from the Volga and give himself more of a chance of staying there.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑或许能让罗季姆采夫将防线进一步推离伏尔加河，从而为自己在那里的坚守赢得更多胜算。

sentences.en: So from late September all the way through to the end, really, that's the kind of fighting that the Russians employed in the heart of the city
sentences.zh: 因此，从9月下旬一直到最后，这确实是俄军在市中心

sentences.en: and in the factory districts to retake these buildings.
sentences.zh: 和工厂区采用的战斗方式，用来重新夺回这些建筑。

sentences.en: So Pavlov was just part of this.
sentences.zh: 所以巴甫洛夫只是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And the house that Dominic was talking about was a house that stuck out.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克刚才谈到的那座房子是一栋突出的建筑。

sentences.en: It was a huge four-story apartment block.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋巨大的四层公寓楼。

sentences.en: Could probably take at least 200 people.
sentences.zh: 大概至少能容纳200人。

sentences.en: Had over 100 rooMs.
sentences.zh: 拥有100多个房间。

sentences.en: Had a reinforced concrete basement as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一个钢筋混凝土的地下室。

sentences.en: And before the war, it had been one of these new modern blocks that had been built for specialists who worked in the factory districts,
sentences.zh: 在战前，它是为工厂区的专家们建造的现代新型街区之一，

sentences.en: the middle managers, directors, and important party officials.
sentences.zh: 包括中层管理者、厂长和重要的党政官员。

sentences.en: So before the war, it was a place you wanted to live in.
sentences.zh: 所以在战前，这是个你做梦都想住进去的地方。

sentences.en: But during the war, not.
sentences.zh: 但在战争期间，可就不是了。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，一点没错。

sentences.en: By the war, not.
sentences.zh: 到了战争时期，绝对不是。

sentences.en: And so the Germans had taken it.
sentences.zh: 于是德军占领了它。

sentences.en: It was one of their main places that they had taken around the square.
sentences.zh: 这是他们在广场周围占领的主要据点之一。

sentences.en: They already had all the buildings on the other side of the square and to the side of the square as well.
sentences.zh: 他们已经控制了广场另一侧以及广场侧面的所有建筑。

sentences.en: And this building was seen as a, I suppose, it was a vantage point because it was so high.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑被视为一个，我想说，是一个极佳的俯瞰点，因为它很高。

sentences.en: And it becomes a totem.
sentences.zh: 并且它成了一个图腾。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: And it offered great views across the city.
sentences.zh: 它提供了俯瞰全城的绝佳视野。

sentences.en: You could see the whole length of the city.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到城市的整个长度。

sentences.en: You could see what the Germans were doing in terms of where they were moving to.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到德军在人员调动方面的动向。

sentences.en: It would give the artillery spotters on the roof time to then feed back information to the huge artillery parks that Chukov had built on the eastern shore
sentences.zh: 这使得屋顶的炮兵观察员能够及时将信息反馈给崔可夫在东岸建立的庞大炮兵阵地，

sentences.en: that were landing these huge salvos that were destroying German formations as they lined up.
sentences.zh: 那些阵地倾泻出巨大的齐射火力，在德国部队列队集结时将其摧毁。

sentences.en: Even before they attacked, they would be spotted.
sentences.zh: 甚至在他们发起进攻之前，就会被发现。

sentences.en: And this is one of the reasons why the Germans wanted this kind of house back.
sentences.zh: 这也是德军想要夺回这种房子的原因之一。

sentences.en: So when they lost it to Pavlov's team, and then it became infested with reinforcements and turned into a super fortress, the Germans wanted it back.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们把它失守给巴甫洛夫的小队，随后那里充满增援并变成一个超级堡垒后，德军就更想把它夺回来了。

sentences.en: And that's a very similar story to at least a dozen buildings you could talk about in the centre of the city that was fought over, back and forth, over the following months.
sentences.zh: 这跟你在市中心可以谈论的至少十几栋建筑的情况非常相似，在接下来的几个月里，双方为了它们反复争夺。

sentences.en: So when you say a super fortress, they're installing machine guns.
sentences.zh: 所以当你提到超级堡垒时，他们是在安装机枪。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole place must have been shot to pieces, but it's basically a ruin by now, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个地方肯定被打得稀巴烂，但到目前为止它基本上已经是一片废墟了，对吧？

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the roof's pretty much caved in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，屋顶基本塌了。

sentences.en: Obviously, all the windows are shot out.
sentences.zh: 显然，所有的窗户都被打碎了。

sentences.en: And Ian, it's become a kind of totem for the Soviets.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，它已经成为苏联人的一种图腾。

sentences.en: Is it also something that the Germans feel, we've got to take it?
sentences.zh: 这也是不是让德国人觉得，我们无论如何必须把它拿下来？

sentences.en: Well, that's what I found in the research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我在研究中发现的。

sentences.en: It was never – again, if you look at the official story,
sentences.zh: 它从来都不是——再说一次，如果你看官方的说法，

sentences.en: Paulus himself apparently had it marked on his map that Pavlov's house was a place that they needed to take, but it's not mentioned in any combat diary
sentences.zh: 保卢斯本人显然在他的地图上把巴甫洛夫的房子标为需要攻占的地点，但这并没有在任何作战日记中提及，

sentences.en: of the main German divisions, the two or three German divisions that were operating in that area.
sentences.zh: 即在那个地区作战的两三个德国主力师的作战日记中。

sentences.en: They never talked about it.
sentences.zh: 他们从未提及此事。

sentences.en: The main combat commander whose personal papers I discovered, who was a key figure in the fighting in this area, never mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 那位我发现了其个人文件的主要作战指挥官，他是这一地区战斗的关键人物，也从未提及它。

sentences.en: He talks about other buildings that they fought for, but he didn't talk about Pavlov's house.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了他们为之战斗的其他建筑，但没有谈到巴甫洛夫的房子。

sentences.en: But it was – don't get me wrong, it was essential.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是——别误会我的意思，它至关重要。

sentences.en: They needed to have it.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拥有它。

sentences.en: It was almost their warning system for anything that would happen if the Germans were going to advance towards Radimsev's main line.
sentences.zh: 它几乎成了他们的预警系统，以防德国人向罗季姆采夫的主防线推进时发生任何情况。

sentences.en: He needed that as his almost canary in the gas chamber to warn him what was going on.
sentences.zh: 他需要这个地方，几乎就像毒气室里的金丝雀一样，用来警告他发生了什么。

sentences.en: But you're right, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但你说得对，汤姆。

sentences.en: They'd laid minefields around the building.
sentences.zh: 他们在建筑物周围布设了雷区。

sentences.en: It was heavily barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 布满了厚重的铁丝网。

sentences.en: They'd moved in heavy machine guns.
sentences.zh: 他们搬进了重机枪。

sentences.en: They'd moved in teams of tank destroyers on the roof.
sentences.zh: 他们在屋顶部署了反坦克小组。

sentences.en: It was pretty impregnable.
sentences.zh: 它可以说是坚不可摧。

sentences.en: So why – I mean, Pavlov's house becomes famous, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么——我的意思是，巴甫洛夫的房子变得很有名，不是吗？

sentences.en: Is it famous during the battle, or is it only famous afterwards?
sentences.zh: 它是在战役期间就出名了，还是只有在战后才出名的？

sentences.en: Because I think – isn't it taken up by a newspaper called Stalin's Banner?
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得——它是不是被一份叫《斯大林旗帜》的报纸报道了？

sentences.en: Great name for a newspaper.
sentences.zh: 报纸的名字真棒。

sentences.en: Tell where that's coming from.
sentences.zh: 讲讲这个名字的来历。

sentences.en: I think it's political leanings, very clear.
sentences.zh: 我想它的政治倾向非常明确。

sentences.en: So Stalin's Banner is basically the Russian Guardian.
sentences.zh: 所以《斯大林旗帜》基本上就是俄国人的《卫报》。

sentences.en: It's – and it creates – I'm right in thinking that this is long after the battle and it basically creates Pavlov's house as a kind of –
sentences.zh: 它是——它创造了——我没记错的话，这是在战役很久之后，它基本上把巴甫洛夫的房子塑造为了一种——

sentences.en: an emblem of Soviet fellowship and bravery and – Because it's all about how it's not just Russians, is it?
sentences.zh: 苏联同胞情谊和英勇精神的象征，而且——因为这完全关乎它不仅仅是俄罗斯人，对吧？

sentences.en: It's people from across the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 它是来自整个苏联各地的人们。

sentences.en: It's a band of happy brothers.
sentences.zh: 这是一群快乐的兄弟连。

sentences.en: The Red Army during the Second World War really expanded their propaganda tentacles into their formations.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战期间的红军确实将他们的宣传触角延伸到了各支部队中。

sentences.en: There was over 1,300 newspapers and journals published, created and published across the Red Army, across every territory.
sentences.zh: 红军在各个领土出版、创建并发行了1300多份报纸和期刊。

sentences.en: So that's where you've got people like Ilya Ehrenberg and Valizzi Grossman and these sort of iconic figures.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么会有像伊利亚·爱伦堡和瓦西里·格罗斯曼这样的人物，以及诸如此类的标志性人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, there were over, I think, 5,000 reporters that would work on these journals and newspapers.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，当时有超过，我想有5000名记者为这些期刊和报纸工作。

sentences.en: And of that 5,000, over 900 were professional writers as Orenberg and obviously Vasili Grossman.
sentences.zh: 在这5000人中，有900多名是专业作家，比如爱伦堡，当然还有瓦西里·格罗斯曼。

sentences.en: So they were part of this organized, dedicated setup to report the stories that boosted morale, gave any kind of defeat a certain slant, that it didn't seem so catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们是有组织、专门的机构的一部分，负责报道那些能够振奋士气的故事，给任何形式的失败进行某种修饰，让它看起来不那么灾难性。

sentences.en: And Stalingrad, as you said right at the beginning, became a metaphor for almost the soul of the Russian during that part of the great patriotic war.
sentences.zh: 正如你在一开始所说的那样，斯大林格勒在伟大的卫国战争的那个时期，几乎成了俄罗斯人灵魂的隐喻。

sentences.en: We cannot give Stalin up.
sentences.zh: 我们不能放弃斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: It's a breathing, living city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座有呼吸、有生命的城市。

sentences.en: It's not a dead city.
sentences.zh: 它不是一座死城。

sentences.en: We are fighting for it.
sentences.zh: 我们在为它而战。

sentences.en: We are fighting for the soul.
sentences.zh: 我们在为灵魂而战。

sentences.en: And we are defending Mother Russia and Mother Volga.
sentences.zh: 我们在保卫伟大的俄罗斯母亲和伏尔加河母亲。

sentences.en: And that's the kind of attitude that was taken.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时所采取的态度。

sentences.en: So, Ian, I listened to the podcast that our sister podcast, We Have Ways, did on Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊恩，我听了我们的兄弟播客《我们有办法》制作的关于斯大林格勒的节目。

sentences.en: And they had an interview with a very interesting, I think, creator of the Museum of the Second World War in Dresden.
sentences.zh: 他们采访了一位非常有趣的，我想是德累斯顿第二次世界大战博物馆的创建者。

sentences.en: And he scoffed at the idea.
sentences.zh: 而他对这种观点嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: We don't have scoffing on our podcast, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们的播客里可不兴嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: Well, he didn't scoff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他倒也没有嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: He was politely skeptical of the idea that Stalingrad had resonance for the Soviets and for Stalin himself because it was Stalin's city, because of its name.
sentences.zh: 他只是礼貌地怀疑，斯大林格勒对苏联人和斯大林本人具有共鸣，是因为它是斯大林的城市，是因为它的名字。

sentences.en: What's your take on that?
sentences.zh: 你对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: I think I would say inside the city, those that were fighting for it, definitely I would agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说，在城市内部，那些为它战斗的人，我绝对同意这一点。

sentences.en: I think they weren't fighting for Stalin.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们不是为了斯大林而战。

sentences.en: They weren't fighting for any kind of notional idea that they were saving Russia.
sentences.zh: 他们不是为了拯救俄罗斯这种虚无缥缈的概念而战。

sentences.en: I think, as any combat soldiers would say, fighting in any kind of horrific situation like this, they're fighting for each other.
sentences.zh: 我认为，正如任何战斗士兵所说的那样，在任何可怕的局势中战斗，他们都是为了彼此而战。

sentences.en: You're doing it for your friends.
sentences.zh: 你是为了你的朋友而战。

sentences.en: But the broader, the propaganda thing, the spin, how is the Soviet press, how is the Soviet media spinning it?
sentences.zh: 但从宏观层面、宣传层面、舆论包装来看，苏联报刊、苏联媒体是如何进行舆论引导的？

sentences.en: The story was taken up on the 31st of October.
sentences.zh: 这个故事是在10月31日被采纳的。

sentences.en: It was first mentioned.
sentences.zh: 它首次被提及。

sentences.en: By then, the battle had moved to the north, the factory district.
sentences.zh: 到那时，战斗已经转移到了北部，也就是工厂区。

sentences.en: The south of the city had already been captured weeks before.
sentences.zh: 城市的南部在几周前就已经被攻占了。

sentences.en: The central part was pretty much 90% occupied by the Germans.
sentences.zh: 中部地区差不多90%都被德军占领了。

sentences.en: There was only that sliver of a few hundred meters depth from the Volga that was still occupied by Radims' forces.
sentences.zh: 只剩下从伏尔加河算起只有几百米深狭长地带，依然由罗季姆采夫的部队占领。

sentences.en: Paulus was now under instruction that you've taken those two bits.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯当时接到指示，你们已经拿下了那两个部分。

sentences.en: The final bit is to now take the factory district.
sentences.zh: 最后的部分就是现在拿下工厂区。

sentences.en: And that's where the fighting had moved to.
sentences.zh: 战斗已经转移到那里去了。

sentences.en: So Pavlov's house and the 9th of January square was quite quiet at the time.
sentences.zh: 所以当时巴甫洛夫的房子和一月九日广场相当安静。

sentences.en: And that's when the reporters, I suppose, felt it safe to move in and do some interviews.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我想记者们才觉得可以安全地搬进去做一些采访。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what happened.
sentences.zh: 事实也正是如此。

sentences.en: So as I say in the book, this correspondent for the newspaper, six-page newspaper or newsletter for the 62nd Army was called Stalin's Banner.
sentences.zh: 正如我在书中所说，第62集团军这份六页纸的报纸或简报的这位通讯员，名字就叫《斯大林旗帜》。

sentences.en: And a lieutenant, Julie Shapurin, happened to be given permission to go into the house.
sentences.zh: 而有一位中尉朱利安·沙普林，碰巧获准进入了这栋房子。

sentences.en: And he was the one who actually gave the term in the first article about it on the 31st of October, the house of Pavlov.
sentences.zh: 他实际上也是在 10 月 31 日关于该事件的第一篇文章中，第一个将其冠以“巴甫洛夫的房子”这一名称的人。

sentences.en: And in that, he then waxes lyrical about the tropes that have survived all these decades long, about there was a few of them.
sentences.zh: 在文中，他随后对那些历经数十年流传至今的英雄传说大加赞赏，并谈到了其中几位人物。

sentences.en: They were a band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 他们情同手足。

sentences.en: They came from this huge ethnic mix that represented the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他们来自代表了整个苏联的庞大民族大熔炉。

sentences.en: So Tatars, Chechens, Tajiks, and ironically Ukrainians, that would hold off this relentless horde of German infantry, aerial attacks and armoured attacks for the next 58 days.
sentences.zh: 因此，有鞑靼人、车臣人、塔吉克斯坦人，具有讽刺意味的是还有乌克兰人，他们在接下来的 58 天里，死死抵挡住了德国步兵、空袭和装甲部队一波又一波的猛烈进攻。

sentences.en: And is this rubbish, ultimately?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是不是无稽之谈？

sentences.en: It's inflated.
sentences.zh: 这是被夸大了的。

sentences.en: It happened to a degree.
sentences.zh: 这种事确实在一定程度上发生过。

sentences.en: But like any fight that was going on in the city, as we talked about earlier on, you capture a house or you capture a room or a floor in a house,
sentences.zh: 但就像我们在前面讨论过的，城里发生的任何战斗都一样，你占领了一栋房子，或者占领了房子里的一个房间、一层楼，

sentences.en: you might give it up within 12 hours, and then you might retake it again.
sentences.zh: 你可能在 12 小时内就会失守，然后又可能会把它夺回来。

sentences.en: And this goes back and forward, back and forward over the days and the weeks of this fighting.
sentences.zh: 在这场战斗的日日夜夜里，这样的反复拉锯一直在上演。

sentences.en: And that's why it became a meat grinder.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它被称为绞肉机。

sentences.en: The house itself, they took it.
sentences.zh: 房子本身，他们确实占领了。

sentences.en: But by my reading of the accounts that were written down and just stored in the Panorama Museum's archives, and that's not just the ordinary soldiers who fought with Pavlov,
sentences.zh: 但根据我的解读，那些被记录下来并存放在全景博物馆档案中的记载——不仅仅是与巴甫洛夫并肩作战的普通士兵的记录，

sentences.en: but his commanding officer and then the chain of command right up to regimental level that was in charge of operations in the area, they moved in a lot of troops.
sentences.zh: 还有他的指挥官，以及一直到负责该地区军事行动的团级指挥链的记录——表明他们调入了大量的部队。

sentences.en: That's how they turned it into a fortress.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们把它变成堡垒的方式。

sentences.en: And that's how they were turning the other houses into fortresses.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们将其他房屋变成堡垒的方式。

sentences.en: The whole point of which was, yes, they're going to attack us.
sentences.zh: 其核心意义在于，是的，他们要来进攻我们。

sentences.en: And primarily they're going to attack us via aerial attack because that was their best weapon and artillery barrages.
sentences.zh: 而且他们主要会通过空袭来进攻我们，因为那是他们最好的武器，还有猛烈的炮火轰炸。

sentences.en: And that does cause casualties.
sentences.zh: 这确实造成了人员伤亡。

sentences.en: But as soon as the casualties were shipped out, more reinforcements come in.
sentences.zh: 但一旦伤亡人员被运走，就会有更多的增援部队开进来。

sentences.en: So it's not really a band of brothers.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实并不是什么生死之交的兄弟连。

sentences.en: It's a shifting.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不断轮替的过程。

sentences.en: It's homogenous.
sentences.zh: 它是由各种成分组成的人群。

sentences.en: And there's an awful lot of troops.
sentences.zh: 而且那里有数量惊人的部队。

sentences.en: And Pavlov himself, am I right in thinking that Pavlov wasn't the commander?
sentences.zh: 巴甫洛夫本人，我没记错的话，巴甫洛夫并不是指挥官对吗？

sentences.en: The commander was a man called Afanasiev, Lieutenant Afanasiev.
sentences.zh: 指挥官是一个叫阿法纳西夫的人，阿法纳西夫中尉。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he came in within 48 hours of Pavlov's storm team taking the house.
sentences.zh: 对，所以在巴甫洛夫的突击队攻占这栋房子后的 48 小时内他就赶到了。

sentences.en: And again, there's conjecture on whether they actually took the house by fighting.
sentences.zh: 同样，关于他们究竟是不是通过战斗攻占这栋房子的，目前还有所推测。

sentences.en: There's some German stories I've read is there was actually no one there.
sentences.zh: 我读过一些德国方面的说法，称当时那里其实一个人也没有。

sentences.en: The Germans had vacated it.
sentences.zh: 德国人已经撤出了。

sentences.en: That's not such a good story there, is it?
sentences.zh: 那听起来就没那么精彩了，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: But the legend is they were there and they took it room by room and they succeeded.
sentences.zh: 但传说他们当时确实在那里，并且挨个房间争夺，最终取得了成功。

sentences.en: So Afanasiev took over 48 hours later.
sentences.zh: 所以在 48 小时后，阿法纳西夫接管了指挥权。

sentences.en: He was the one who led the first of a number of reinforcement columns into the house.
sentences.zh: 他率领了首批多支增援部队开进这栋房子。

sentences.en: So, Ian, it's a meat grinder.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊恩，这就是一个绞肉机。

sentences.en: The Germans and the Russians are kind of tearing chunks out of each other.
sentences.zh: 德国人和俄国人简直是在互相从对方身上撕下一块块肉。

sentences.en: Nothing much seems to be happening except that everyone's dying.
sentences.zh: 似乎什么实质进展都没有，除了每个人都在不断牺牲。

sentences.en: But then something does change.
sentences.zh: 但随后，情况确实发生了变化。

sentences.en: And this is Operation Uranus.
sentences.zh: 这就是“天王星行动”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this had been actually first talked about during the really dark days of early September when the Germans were first investing the city and they'd already reduced it to rubble.
sentences.zh: 事实上，早在 9 月初那段最黑暗的日子里，当德国人首次对这座城市形成合围并将其化为一片废墟时，就已经有人开始讨论这个计划了。

sentences.en: And it was a case of, and Zhukov hadn't even been given his command yet.
sentences.zh: 当时甚至朱可夫都还没被授予指挥权。

sentences.en: And this was Georgi Zhukov.
sentences.zh: 这就是格奥尔基·朱可夫。

sentences.en: At the time, he wasn't Marshal Zhukov yet.
sentences.zh: 当时他还不是朱可夫元帅。

sentences.en: He would be a year or so later.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后他才被授予元帅军衔。

sentences.en: But at the time, he was a general, but he was still deputy supreme commander.
sentences.zh: 但当时他是一名将军，而且仍然是副最高统帅。

sentences.en: And he was the one reporting to Stalin in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他是那个向莫斯科的斯大林汇报的人。

sentences.en: And with his colleague, Vasilevsky, they were outlining the predicament they were in.
sentences.zh: 他和同僚华西列夫斯基一起，勾勒出了他们当时面临的困境。

sentences.en: And the Germans were still pushing towards the Volga and they were going to seize Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 当时德军仍在向伏尔加河推进，企图攻占斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: And as well as getting a flea in their ear from Stalin, who obviously didn't want to have this happen,
sentences.zh: 除了遭到斯大林的一通训斥——斯大林显然极力避免这种情况发生——

sentences.en: they had the, I was going to say the guts, they had the ability to actually sit him down
sentences.zh: 他们有——我本来想说有这个胆量，他们有这个能力让斯大林坐下来，

sentences.en: and mention that they had this plan as military strategists, great military strategists, both of them were.
sentences.zh: 作为军事战略家——他们两人都是伟大的军事战略家——向他提出他们制定好的这个计划。

sentences.en: They could see how overextended the German lines were now from their main base where they'd started from.
sentences.zh: 他们能看出，从德军出发的主基地算起，他们的战线现在拉得有多么长，推进得有多么深入。

sentences.en: And they had very weak flanks.
sentences.zh: 而且他们的侧翼非常薄弱。

sentences.en: So it's all about the trucks.
sentences.zh: 所以关键全在卡车上。

sentences.en: It's all about the trucks.
sentences.zh: 全都在于卡车。

sentences.en: So about the trucks, and as had been said, the bulk of the fighting going towards the Volga was being done by German troops, infantry and armour, and the Luftwaffe, like I said.
sentences.zh: 所以关于卡车，正如刚才所说，向伏尔加河推进的主力战斗是由德军部队、步兵和装甲部队，以及就像我说的德国空军来完成的。

sentences.en: But their flanks were being guarded by their Axis allies.
sentences.zh: 但他们的侧翼是由其轴心国盟友来守护的。

sentences.en: And their Axis allies are not strong, right?
sentences.zh: 而他们的轴心国盟友并不强大，对吧？

sentences.en: They're not strong.
sentences.zh: 他们并不强大。

sentences.en: They had great fighting spirit.
sentences.zh: 他们有着极高的战斗精神。

sentences.en: And that's what I've seen in a lot of the records I've read.
sentences.zh: 这也是我在读过的许多档案记录中所看到的。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, a lot of them did flee when Uranus started.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很显然，“天王星行动”一开始，他们当中确实有很多人逃跑了。

sentences.en: But if you're an infantryman on the frozen steppe and you haven't been fed properly in weeks and you haven't got the anti-tank guns you're required to fend off a T-34,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个冰冻草原上的步兵，已经好几个星期没吃饱饭了，手里也没有抵御 T-34 坦克所必需的反坦克炮，

sentences.en: when you see hundreds of them coming through the foggy mist, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 当你看到成百上千辆坦克穿过茫茫大雾驶来时，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: And they did put up a fight for a day or two days, I think, in the north when the first section started.
sentences.zh: 我想，在北部第一阶段行动刚开始的那一两天里，他们确实进行了一场抵抗。

sentences.en: But it's a weight of numbers and a weight of firepower.
sentences.zh: 但敌人的数量和火力实在太庞大了。

sentences.en: They're mostly Romanians.
sentences.zh: 他们大多是罗马尼亚人。

sentences.en: Are they Romanians, Hungarians?
sentences.zh: 他们是罗马尼亚人，还是匈牙利人？

sentences.en: And primarily Romanians were guarding the flanks with the Italians and the Hungarians too.
sentences.zh: 主要由罗马尼亚人连同意大利人和匈牙利人一起防守侧翼。

sentences.en: But predominantly, famously, the main breaks in the line at the beginning were from the Romanians that were guarding the flanks, in the north especially.
sentences.zh: 但最主要也是最著名的是，战线在初期被突破的地方，主要是在北部负责防守侧翼的罗马尼亚军队防区。

sentences.en: But Ian, you said it was tanks.
sentences.zh: 但伊恩，你刚才说是坦克。

sentences.en: But also, I gather from your book, Cossack horse cavalry.
sentences.zh: 不过据我从你的书中了解到的，还有哥萨克骑兵。

sentences.en: Great scare tactic.
sentences.zh: 极佳的威慑战术。

sentences.en: And they can travel well in snow.
sentences.zh: 而且他们在雪地里行动自如。

sentences.en: They're well-provisions.
sentences.zh: 他们的物资补给很充足。

sentences.en: Yeah, thousands upon thousands of Cossack columns.
sentences.zh: 是的，成千上万的哥萨克纵队。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I had no idea that at the Battle of Stalingrad, the Cossacks on their horses played a key role.
sentences.zh: 所以我的意思是，我以前根本不知道在斯大林格勒战役中，骑着马的哥萨克人发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: Well, that's in the steppe, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那是发生在草原上的事。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something out of the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那简直像是 18 世纪的战争场景。

sentences.en: It's not in the city itself.
sentences.zh: 那不是在城市里面发生的。

sentences.en: It's out on the steppe.
sentences.zh: 那是在广阔的草原上。

sentences.en: Because you've got to remember that this frontier ran for hundreds of miles.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须记住，这条前线绵延了数百英里。

sentences.en: So this is the encircling process.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个合围的过程。

sentences.en: So this is – they're coming around and they're kind of bottling the Germans up.
sentences.zh: 这就是——他们从周围包抄过来，有点像把德国人装进瓶子里一样封锁起来。

sentences.en: And you compare it to the Battle of Cannes, Hannibal's great victory over the Romans.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它比作坎尼会战，那是汉尼拔对罗马人取得的伟大胜利。

sentences.en: But at Cannes, Hannibal's army was smaller than the Roman army that they envelop.
sentences.zh: 但在坎尼会战中，汉尼拔的军队规模要小于他们所包围的罗马军队。

sentences.en: But presumably by this point at Stalingrad, the Russians are starting to really outnumber the Germans, are they?
sentences.zh: 但可以推测，此时在斯大林格勒，俄国人在数量上真的开始大大超过德国人了，对吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, that's when their reinforcements are really coming online.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是他们的增援部队真正开上战场的时候。

sentences.en: They're being fed into the mix of the big bridgeheads that Zhukov was building up on either flank, north and south of the city.
sentences.zh: 他们被源源不断地投入到朱可夫在城市南北两侧的各个大桥头堡的战局中。

sentences.en: Not just in terms of men.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是在兵力人数上。

sentences.en: They had well over a million men by now, fresh troops, including Cossacks.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，他们拥有远超百万的兵力，全都是生力军，其中还包括哥萨克人。

sentences.en: But you had hundreds of tanks.
sentences.zh: 而且你们拥有数百辆坦克。

sentences.en: And they'd rebuilt the Soviet Air Force.
sentences.zh: 他们还重建了苏联空军。

sentences.en: So they had well over a thousand planes now that could contest the skies over the city as well as in and around the areas that they were going to attack in a pincer movement from north and south.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在拥有远远超过一千架飞机，不仅能够争夺城市上空的制空权，还能在他们准备从南北两翼实施钳形攻势的作战区域及周边地区发挥作用。

sentences.en: And so how long after starting Operation Uranus did the Germans find themselves surrounded?
sentences.zh: 那么，从“天王星行动”开始到德国人发现自己被合围，隔了多久？

sentences.en: Within days.
sentences.zh: 几天之内。

sentences.en: So it was launched in the north on the 19th, the following day from the south.
sentences.zh: 行动于 19 日在北部发起，第二天在南部发起。

sentences.en: And by the 23rd, they met up famously at a transport hub, Kalach, which was roughly around 40 to 50 kilometers deep into the German lines and way behind Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 到了 23 日，他们在一个交通枢纽卡拉奇胜利会师，这里深入德军防线大约 40 到 50 公里，位于斯大林格勒的后方很远处。

sentences.en: And that's where they met.
sentences.zh: 他们就在那里会师了。

sentences.en: And that's where the Germans realized they were in a tricky situation.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那里，德国人意识到自己陷入了进退维谷的困境。

sentences.en: And are they taken, are the Germans taken completely by surprise by this?
sentences.zh: 德国人是被这一切完全打了个措手不及吗？

sentences.en: Have they not seen it coming at all?
sentences.zh: 他们之前一点都没有察觉到风声吗？

sentences.en: They'd had some warnings, but I don't think they realized.
sentences.zh: 他们确实收到过一些警告，但我不认为他们意识到了严重性。

sentences.en: There wasn't the belief, certainly there wasn't a belief in the upper echelons of the high command where Hitler was operating,
sentences.zh: 当时绝对没有这种信念，尤其是希特勒所在的最高统帅部高层，

sentences.en: that they would have not just the resources to attack, but they would have learned from the Germans' use of combined arMs.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅不相信苏军有进攻的资源，而且不相信苏军能学会德国人协同作战的战术。

sentences.en: This was properly the first time that the Russians used combined forces.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是俄国人第一次真正使用诸兵种合成军队。

sentences.en: So air attacks met by then huge artillery bombardments.
sentences.zh: 即空袭配合随后规模巨大的炮火轰炸。

sentences.en: Then the armor goes in and then the infantry follows up.
sentences.zh: 接着装甲部队突击，随后步兵跟进。

sentences.en: They hadn't been doing that before.
sentences.zh: 他们以前并没有这样做过。

sentences.en: This was the first time that it all worked.
sentences.zh: 这是所有环节第一次完美运转。

sentences.en: It clicked and it had incredible results.
sentences.zh: 一切严丝合缝，并取得了惊人的成果。

sentences.en: So Hitler, ironically, 11 days before the Soviets launched this fantastic kind of pincer operation, he has gone in front of his old fighters in the beer hall in Munich.
sentences.zh: 所以极具讽刺意味的是，就在苏联人发动这种绝妙的钳形攻势的 11 天前，希特勒还曾前往慕尼黑的啤酒馆，在老战友们面前发表演说。

sentences.en: And he's basically told them, Stalingrad is finished.
sentences.zh: 他基本上对他们说，斯大林格勒已经结束了。

sentences.en: We're just mopping up with the city as ours, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 我们只是在做最后的清剿，这座城市已经是我们的了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And obviously the question that's always hung over the last, so that the horrendous last weeks, last two months really, of the Battle of Stalingrad is,
sentences.zh: 显然，一直萦绕在斯大林格勒战役最后阶段——也就是那可怕的最后几周、实际上是最后两个月——上空的问题是，

sentences.en: is the Sixth Army, they pretty much know straight away they've been encircled, don't they?
sentences.zh: 第六军队几乎立刻就知道自己被合围了，对吗？

sentences.en: And they say, should we break out now of the encirclement back to the West, link up with the rest of the German forces, or are we just going to stay here and somehow fight it out?
sentences.zh: 他们提出，我们现在是应该立刻突围退回西方，与其余的德军会合，还是就在这里固守待援，无论如何打到底？

sentences.en: And Hitler says, well, you absolutely have to stay.
sentences.zh: 而希特勒说，不，你们绝对必须留下来。

sentences.en: You cannot retreat.
sentences.zh: 你们绝不能撤退。

sentences.en: Show national socialist spirit.
sentences.zh: 展现出国家社会主义的精神。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: I mean, there's so many questions about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于这一点有太多的疑问了。

sentences.en: Is this Hitler's ideological blindness?
sentences.zh: 这究竟是希特勒在意识形态上的盲目固执吗？

sentences.en: Do his generals know that it's folly?
sentences.zh: 他的将领们难道不知道这是愚蠢的做法吗？

sentences.en: And I suppose third, if he had said, actually, you know what, break out, get back to the West, get back to the rest of the troops, could they have even done it?
sentences.zh: 我想第三个问题是，如果他当时说，好吧，听着，突围吧，撤回西方，回到大部队身边，他们当时还能做到吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a big ask in the weather as well, especially when you're up against so many fresh troops and tanks and a revitalized Air Force Two.
sentences.zh: 是的，在那种天气条件下这绝对是个极其艰难的要求，特别是当你还要面对数不清的生力军、坦克以及一支同样恢复了生气的苏联空军时。

sentences.en: They probably would have done it, but it's speculation on how much would be left by the time they've done it.
sentences.zh: 他们可能本来是能做到的，但这只是一种假设，即等他们突围成功时还剩多少兵力。

sentences.en: Hitler is famous for not saying they couldn't do it, and he slept on it overnight,
sentences.zh: 希特勒一向以固执己见著称，他并没有直接说他们做不到，而是思索了一夜，

sentences.en: and then he's persuaded by Goering, or some of Goering's logistical commanders as well, that an airlift was possible.
sentences.zh: 随后被戈林或戈林手下的一些后勤指挥官说服了，他们声称空中补给是可行的。

sentences.en: And it had worked the year before.
sentences.zh: 而且前一年这招曾奏效过。

sentences.en: So once we had the, after Barbarossa and the Russian winter counteroffensive, there had been various pockets that had been isolated once Hitler had said stand and fight.
sentences.zh: 因此，自从巴巴罗萨行动和俄国冬季反攻之后，每当希特勒下令坚守不退时，确实曾有一些被孤立的口袋阵。

sentences.en: And these had been successfully, I mean, we're talking army groups, not a few thousand men,
sentences.zh: 这些部队都曾成功突围——我们说的是集团军群，而不是几千人的部队，

sentences.en: huge armies of about 70 to 80,000 men that had been surrounded by the Russian counteroffensive, had been resupplied and fought their way out.
sentences.zh: 那是被俄国反击部队合围的大约七八万人的庞大军队，当时得到了物资补给并最终杀出了一条血路。

sentences.en: So it had worked.
sentences.zh: 所以这种方法以前成功过。

sentences.en: So he, on the one hand, he wanted to believe what he was being told by Goering, who had been out of favour and was now trying to get back in favour,
sentences.zh: 因此他一方面愿意相信戈林的话——戈林此前已经失宠，现在正极力想重新博得信任——

sentences.en: who was promising him, I can get together enough transport planes to supply the Sixth Army, which was bogus from the start.
sentences.zh: 戈林向他保证，我能凑集足够多的运输机来为第六军队提供补给，这个承诺从一开始就是荒谬的。

sentences.en: But equally, as Hitler surprisingly admitted to his chief of staff, he was in the operations room,
sentences.zh: 但同样地，正如希特勒令人惊讶地向他的参谋长承认的那样，当时他正身处作战室内，

sentences.en: and he's pointing to obviously where the situation where they're in at the moment, this pincer's closed, and he's pointing to Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 他指着地图上他们目前所处的局势、那个已经合拢的巨大钳形包围圈，然后指着斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: He said, if we retreat from there, we are never getting back there.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我们从那里撤退，我们就再也回不去了。

sentences.en: He was a realist enough to know that the cost that it had taken to get there, he wouldn't be in the situation to get it again.
sentences.zh: 他足够现实，深知当初为了打到那里付出了怎样巨大的代价，他将再也没有机会重返故地。

sentences.en: So what's the possible endgame in, though, in which they, because they can't hold out?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然他们根本无法坚守，他们可能的最终结局会是什么呢？

sentences.en: Or does he think?
sentences.zh: 或者他是怎么想的？

sentences.en: There's the other army, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 还有另一支军队，不是吗？

sentences.en: So there's the army to the south.
sentences.zh: 所以南线有军队。

sentences.en: But again, I think that was a gesture, more than a specific plan.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，我认为这只是一种姿态，而非具体的计划。

sentences.en: I don't think it was ever a realistic option.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这曾经是一个切合实际的选择。

sentences.en: So this is Operation Winter Storm, is that right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是“冬风行动”，对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and that was von Manstein, who'd been promoted to field marshal because he'd successfully conquered the Crimea with the 11th Army.
sentences.zh: 对，那是曼施坦因，他因成功用第11集团军征服了克里米亚而被晋升为元帅。

sentences.en: He was then parachuted in, as he would be in future operations through the war.
sentences.zh: 他随后空降到前线，就像他在战争期间以后的行动中一样。

sentences.en: He was a very able, talented commander.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常能干、有才华的指挥官。

sentences.en: He was given a couple of fresh divisions and some battered survivors that had managed to retreat west and get back to the lines from the encirclement.
sentences.zh: 他得到了一些生力军和一些被打残的幸存者，他们设法向西撤退并从包围圈回到了防线。

sentences.en: And these were used to try and batter a way through.
sentences.zh: 这些部队被用来试图强行冲出一条路。

sentences.en: He tried it.
sentences.zh: 他试过了。

sentences.en: It began 12th of December, but again, they just weren't appreciative of, A, the Russian winter and the kind of forces that they were now facing.
sentences.zh: 它始于12月12日，但同样，他们根本没有意识到，第一，俄罗斯的冬天，第二，他们现在所面对的部队类型。

sentences.en: Because they were all wearing the wrong shoes.
sentences.zh: 因为他们都穿着错误的鞋子。

sentences.en: Well, no, but the Russians had deliberately, by the time they'd done the encirclement, they then brought in fresh reinforcements to really solidify that line,
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是的，但俄罗斯人在完成包围圈的时候，刻意引入了新鲜的增援部队来真正巩固那条防线，

sentences.en: looking out from Stalingrad to the new frontier the Germans had, whilst the forces surrounding Stalingrad would then reduce it.
sentences.zh: 从斯大林格勒向德国人的新前沿望去，而包围斯大林格勒的军队随后将削弱它。

sentences.en: So then they're in this, what are they called, the Kessel, the Kessel, which is sort of shrinking by the day, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以他们现在身处这个，它们叫什么来着，“克塞尔”（Kessel），即包围圈，基本上每天都在缩小。

sentences.en: And I guess at this point, the Germans are probably losing as many men to frostbite and cold and starvation as they are to Russian fire.
sentences.zh: 我想在这个时候，德国人因冻伤、寒冷和饥饿而损失的人数，可能和死于俄军火力下的不相上下。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, as we were talking about, they'd been promised X amounts of provisions and supplies by the Luftwaffe or by Göring.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如我们之前讨论的，他们曾被空军或戈林承诺过X数量的物资和补给。

sentences.en: And the Luftwaffe, the transport planes that they tried to scrape together from all different theatres of operations to try and achieve this, it was never going to happen.
sentences.zh: 而空军，那些他们从各个不同战区拼凑起来试图实现这一目标的运输机，是永远无法成功的。

sentences.en: Even on a good day, they delivered half the tonnage that the Sixth Army needed, because this is over 300,000 men trapped in this Kessel.
sentences.zh: 哪怕是在天气好的日子里，他们运送的吨位也只有第六集团军所需的一半，因为这是有30万大军被困在这个包围圈里。

sentences.en: They need everything that you need to survive, not just arms and armaments.
sentences.zh: 他们需要生存所需的一切，不仅仅是武器和军火。

sentences.en: So you're right, the operations that were subsequently then happening over the coming weeks, going into 1943, into January,
sentences.zh: 所以你说得对，随后在接下来的几周里，一直到1943年、19世纪1月展开的行动，

sentences.en: was simply to isolate specific areas of the pocket to carve it up and isolate those pockets to then easily reduce them further.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了孤立口袋的具体区域，将其分割并孤立这些口袋，以便随后进一步轻松地消灭它们。

sentences.en: It did cost the Russians thousands and thousands of troops to do this.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人为此付出了成千上万士兵的代价。

sentences.en: But they can afford it.
sentences.zh: 但他们承担得起。

sentences.en: They can afford it, and the Germans were putting up a good fight.
sentences.zh: 他们承担得起，而且德国人在进行顽强的抵抗。

sentences.en: And in the middle of this, Ian, you have these incredibly harrowing, actually kind of oddly haunting scenes of the Germans at Christmas.
sentences.zh: 而在这一切的中间，伊恩，你看到了德国人在圣诞节那些极其痛苦、甚至有点诡异的难忘场景。

sentences.en: They try to cut down trees with Christmas trees.
sentences.zh: 他们试着用树木当圣诞树砍伐。

sentences.en: They light candles.
sentences.zh: 他们点燃蜡烛。

sentences.en: They think about their families back home.
sentences.zh: 他们思念远方的家人。

sentences.en: They sing hymns and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们唱着赞美诗之类的。

sentences.en: So I had something like this about this in my kids' book that I did about the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 所以我为我写的一本关于第二次世界大战的儿童书写过类似的内容。

sentences.en: And when my son was reading in draft, he said to me, he was then, I think, eight, and he said,
sentences.zh: 当我的儿子在读初稿时，他对我说了，当时他我想有八岁，他说，

sentences.en: God, this is the first time I've realised the Germans were people too.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这是我第一次意识到德国人也是人。

sentences.en: I almost feel sorry for them.
sentences.zh: 我几乎有点同情他们了。

sentences.en: But you do kind of, it's hard to read that.
sentences.zh: 但你确实会这样，读到这些很难受。

sentences.en: I mean, whenever we read the stories of the Battle of Stalingrad, for obvious reasons, the Germans loom in our imagination as it were the villains.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每当我们阅读斯大林格勒战役的故事时，由于显而易见的原因，德国人在我们的想象中就像是恶棍。

sentences.en: But when you read those stories of them, you know, sort of their eyes full of tears, kind of trying to celebrate Christmas, it's hard.
sentences.zh: 但当你读到那些关于他们的故事时，你知道的，他们眼里含着泪水，试图庆祝圣诞节，这很难受。

sentences.en: Do you think it's hard not to be moved, or am I being too sentimental?
sentences.zh: 你觉得很难不为之所动吗，还是说我太感情用事了？

sentences.en: No, I think it's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 不，我认为这绝对是对的。

sentences.en: It's human nature.
sentences.zh: 这是人性。

sentences.en: I mean, I hugely admire the Russians for what they did and what they suffered.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我极大地钦佩俄罗斯人所做的一切以及他们所承受的痛苦。

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, you can't help it.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我的意思是，你情不自禁。

sentences.en: And you look at the, you know, like I have, you look at some of the drawings that were created, the Christmas cards.
sentences.zh: 你看那些，你知道的，就像我一样，你看一些创作出来的画作，圣诞卡。

sentences.en: I've got several at home here that were supplied to me when I was talking to veterans.
sentences.zh: 我家里有几个，是我和老兵交谈时提供给我的。

sentences.en: Very kindly, they gave them.
sentences.zh: 他们非常善良地把它们送给了我。

sentences.en: They look so sweet and amazing.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来那么甜蜜和惊人。

sentences.en: And they obviously, behind them must be a story of terror and despair.
sentences.zh: 而它们背后显然必然隐藏着恐怖和绝望的故事。

sentences.en: The personal papers I got from Colonel Friedrich Roscoe, who's obviously in charge of a regiment that was in the centre of all this in the city fighting.
sentences.zh: 我从弗里德里希·罗斯科（Friedrich Roscoe）上校那里得到的个人文件，他显然负责市中心所有这一切战斗核心的一个团。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's one of your big characters, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是的，他是你的大人物之一，对吧？

sentences.en: Again, it's heartbreaking.
sentences.zh: 同样，这令人心碎。

sentences.en: He tells an amazing story of how he's standing outside his headquarters and he hadn't told his men it was his birthday.
sentences.zh: 他讲了一个惊人的故事，讲他是如何站在总部外面，没有告诉他的手下今天是他的生日。

sentences.en: And amid the silence of the Russians stopped for a few hours of a barrage, they get out and get some fresh air and they're having a cigarette and he's talking to his officers.
sentences.zh: 在俄罗斯炮击停下几个小时的沉默中，他们出来呼吸新鲜空气，抽着烟，他和军官们谈话。

sentences.en: And he started to be serenaded by the regiment's military band who've scrubbed and donned on their best clothes and come marching out of the basement and sing him happy birthday.
sentences.zh: 他开始听到该团军乐队的伴奏，他们擦洗干净并穿上最好的衣服，从地下室列队走出来为他唱生日快乐歌。

sentences.en: And he's moved to tears.
sentences.zh: 他感动得流泪。

sentences.en: And when you read that, you can't help but feel sorry for their predicament.
sentences.zh: 当你读到这段时，你禁不住会为他们的困境感到难过。

sentences.en: But they had killed a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但他们也杀了很多人的。

sentences.en: Let's bear that in mind.
sentences.zh: 让我们记住这一点。

sentences.en: So, well, just probably a bit of balance there before we get the violins out.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们拿出小提琴拉悲情曲之前，可能需要有一点平衡。

sentences.en: But also the Russians have put out the, that was the talk about the violins out.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯人也放出了，这就是刚才说的小提琴的事。

sentences.en: I was about to say the Russians have the loudspeakers out, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我正要说俄罗斯人架起了高音喇叭，对吧？

sentences.en: And what I always think is the most unbelievably sinister thing, the Russians have got a loudspeaker playing the sound of a clock.
sentences.zh: 而我认为最令人难以置信的阴险的事情是，俄罗斯人放了一个高音喇叭，播放着钟表的声音。

sentences.en: And a voice sort of says in German, every seven seconds, a German dies at Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 有一个声音用德语说，每七秒钟，就有一个德国人在斯大林格勒死去。

sentences.en: God, that is sinister.
sentences.zh: 天哪，太阴险了。

sentences.en: And, I mean, that must have been absolutely terrifying, you know, because the clock ticking and all the time.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，那一定非常可怕，你知道的，因为时钟一直在滴答作响。

sentences.en: Dystopian nightmare.
sentences.zh: 反乌托邦的噩梦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, they were dropping leaflets.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在空投传单。

sentences.en: They were using POWs that they captured that were willing to make speeches or call to their comrades to come over.
sentences.zh: 他们利用抓获的战俘，这些战俘愿意发表演讲或呼吁他们的战友投降。

sentences.en: And towards the end, very much in any kind of huge human disaster, whether it's the Titanic or whatever, you get people that do dreadful things right at the end.
sentences.zh: 到了最后，在任何巨大的灾难中，无论是泰坦尼克号还是别的什么，总会有人在最后关头做出可怕的事情。

sentences.en: And there were.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事情就是这样的。

sentences.en: That kind of psychological warfare worked.
sentences.zh: 那种心理战起作用了。

sentences.en: It convinced whole units to break the line and just walk across the snow into captivity.
sentences.zh: 它说服了整支部队突破防线，直接踩着雪走进战俘营。

sentences.en: Okay, let's, I think we should take a break there.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们该在那里休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, let's have a look at how the Germans surrender, their official surrender.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，让我们看看德国人是如何投降的，他们的官方投降。

sentences.en: And also, I think we should look at how the battle is seen today in Russia and elsewhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 并且，我认为我们应该看看今天在俄罗斯和世界其他地方是如何看待这场战役的。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到“历史其余部分”。

sentences.en: Before the break, we heard how the German defeat in Stalingrad was looking inevitable.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，我们听到了德国在斯大林格勒的失败看起来是如何不可避免的。

sentences.en: But Ian, the first official ultimatum of surrender, so that's official ultimatum sent by the Soviets, by the Red Army High Command to the Germans, comes on the 7th of January.
sentences.zh: 但伊恩，第一个官方的投降最后通牒，也就是苏联人、红军最高统帅部发给德国人的官方最后通牒，是在1月7日发出的。

sentences.en: Have I got that right?
sentences.zh: 我没记错吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Paulus is feeding this back to Hitler in Supreme Headquarters.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯正把这个情况汇报给最高司令部的希特勒。

sentences.en: And they're being discounted one after another.
sentences.zh: 而它们一个接一个地被驳回。

sentences.en: This happens a few times.
sentences.zh: 这种情况发生了好几次。

sentences.en: So there's still communications.
sentences.zh: 所以仍然有通讯。

sentences.en: I mean, how are the communications holding up?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通讯是怎么维持的？

sentences.en: Oh, they had radio communications all the way through until the second to last day of the surrender.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们一直保持着无线电通讯，直到投降前的倒数第二天。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: Because that's how Paulus was then promoted to field commander.
sentences.zh: 因为保卢斯就是这样被晋升为元帅的。

sentences.en: That's how they gave him his promotion to field marshal.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们如何授予他陆军元帅军衔的方式。

sentences.en: And there's a whole welter of promotions to the various officers.
sentences.zh: 还有给各个军官的一大堆晋升。

sentences.en: So basically, which, you know, Paulus says, this is basically an indication I should commit suicide.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，保卢斯说，这基本上是一个暗示我应该自杀的信号。

sentences.en: Yeah, I should kill myself.
sentences.zh: 对，我应该自杀。

sentences.en: So there's that.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样。

sentences.en: And it's just the intensity and the hopelessness of their situation as the ring, the Kessel Ring is shrinking, as it's then broken up into three specific parts, north,
sentences.zh: 随着包围圈在缩小，当它被细分为三个具体部分时，这就是他们处境的强度和绝望，北部、

sentences.en: centre and south.
sentences.zh: 中部和南部。

sentences.en: And the communication between those elements are loSt.
sentences.zh: 这些部队之间的通讯中断了。

sentences.en: And it's what you do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你所做的。

sentences.en: And all the time you've got stragglers moving into these last fortifications, trying to seek shelter, trying to get away from the cold, medical attention,
sentences.zh: 而且一直有散兵游勇进入这些最后的防御工事，试图寻求庇护，试图远离寒冷，寻求医疗救助，

sentences.en: trying to get something to eat.
sentences.zh: 试图找点吃的。

sentences.en: So, Ian, Hitler basically wants them to die like the Spartans at Thermopylae.
sentences.zh: 所以，伊恩，希特勒基本上希望他们像温泉关的斯巴达人一样战死。

sentences.en: But what actually happens?
sentences.zh: 但实际上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Talk us through what the end game is.
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲结局是什么。

sentences.en: Well, the end game, you're right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，结局，你说得对。

sentences.en: He wants them to tie down as many Soviet forces as possible because then it was a strategic matter.
sentences.zh: 他希望他们尽可能多地牵制苏联军队，因为这是一个战略问题。

sentences.en: He still had to try and extricate Army Group A from the Caucasus,
sentences.zh: 他仍然必须设法让A集团军从高加索撤离，

sentences.en: which were in danger of being sealed off if the Russians pushed even further west from where they were surrounding the Stalingrad area.
sentences.zh: 如果俄罗斯人从包围斯大林格勒的地区进一步向西推进，他们将面临被封锁的危险。

sentences.en: They could easily shut the door on Army Group A and then he's got an even bigger disaster on his hands.
sentences.zh: 他们可以轻易地对A集团军关上大门，那他就会面临更大的灾难。

sentences.en: So strategically, it was thought if Paulus can keep going for as long as possible,
sentences.zh: 所以在战略上，人们认为如果保卢斯能尽可能长久地坚持下去，

sentences.en: it ties up several armies that are surrounding Stalingrad and that flank and allows Manstein to extricate as many troops and armor as possible, which is what happened.
sentences.zh: 它就能牵制包围斯大林格勒的几支军队以及那个侧翼，并让曼施坦因撤出尽可能多的军队和装甲部队，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: And he managed to stabilize the front.
sentences.zh: 他设法稳定了前线。

sentences.en: But in Stalingrad itself, yes, it was ground down remorselessly.
sentences.zh: 但在斯大林格勒本身，是的，它被无情地碾压了。

sentences.en: There's tank armies coming in all directions.
sentences.zh: 坦克大军从四面八方涌来。

sentences.en: And don't forget, there's Tukhov's 62nd Army still in the heart of the city fighting for all it's worth to tie down whatever Paulus's forces want to carry on the fight.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，崔可夫的第62集团军仍然在市中心全力战斗，以牵制保卢斯想要继续战斗的任何部队。

sentences.en: And there were quite a few thousand troops that were still prepared to go down fighting to the last bullet as Hitler wanted them to.
sentences.zh: 还有数千名士兵准备按照希特勒的意愿战斗到最后一颗子弹。

sentences.en: He wanted everyone to do that, but they were prepared to do that.
sentences.zh: 他希望每个人都这样做，而他们也准备好这样做了。

sentences.en: And that's what I capture in Rosca's memoir, as in he was just an excellent combat commander.
sentences.zh: 这就是我在罗斯科的回忆录中所捕捉到的，因为他只是一名优秀的战斗指挥官。

sentences.en: And he was the one who put the backbone into that central pocket where Paulus was housed.
sentences.zh: 正是他给保卢斯所在的中心口袋注入了中流砥柱的力量。

sentences.en: And Paulus actually came into his headquarters and took it over as the Sixth Army's headquarters.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯实际上来到了他的总部并接管了它，将其作为第六集团军的总部。

sentences.en: But in charge of the actual perimeter and giving the day-to-day orders was Rosca.
sentences.zh: 但负责实际防御圈并下达日常命令的是罗斯科。

sentences.en: And this is a department store?
sentences.zh: 这是一个百货公司吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the Univirag department store.
sentences.zh: 是的，环球百货公司。

sentences.en: So it really is like something from a – I mean, funnily enough, Pavlov's house that we talked about earlier, I know has been in a video game.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很像某种——我的意思是，有趣的是，我们之前谈到的帕夫洛夫的房子，我知道它曾出现在电子游戏中。

sentences.en: It's been in a level of Call of Duty, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想它出现在《使命召唤》的一个关卡里。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the idea of fighting in the shattered remains of a department store surrounded by this bombed-out city centre, I mean, that's very Call of Duty, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 在百货公司的残垣断壁中战斗的想法，周围是这个被轰炸过的市中心，我的意思是，这非常《使命召唤》，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's literally what's happening.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: They're reduced to this department store.
sentences.zh: 他们沦落到了这个百货公司。

sentences.en: Well, it's a scene from hell.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一场人间炼狱。

sentences.en: And I agree with Tom.
sentences.zh: 我同意汤姆的看法。

sentences.en: It's a hell of their own making.
sentences.zh: 这是他们自己造成的炼狱。

sentences.en: But it's a scene of hell because you've got thousands of dead and dying lying in the basements of this department store.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个炼狱般的场景，因为这家百货公司的地下室里躺着成千上万的死伤者。

sentences.en: And don't forget, right from the beginning of the battle, that had seen some of the most brutal fighting in and around the department store,
sentences.zh: 别忘了，从战役一开始，百货公司内部及其周围就发生了一些最残酷的战斗，

sentences.en: around the square where it was based and nearby the train station.
sentences.zh: 在其所在的广场周围和火车站附近。

sentences.en: That's where the first really titanic struggles were between troops fighting hand-to-hand combat in the buildings and cellars.
sentences.zh: 那是部队在建筑物和地窖中进行肉搏战的第一批真正艰苦的斗争。

sentences.en: So fast forward four months later, it's lunar landscape devastation.
sentences.zh: 所以快进四个月后，这里成了月球表面般的废墟。

sentences.en: And that's their final redoubt.
sentences.zh: 那是他们最后的据点。

sentences.en: And how does the surrender actually happen?
sentences.zh: 投降究竟是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: How is it negotiated?
sentences.zh: 它是如何谈判的？

sentences.en: Well, the official story is a Red Army lieutenant was the first one to make contact and establish that they were offering terMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，官方的说法是，一名红军中尉是第一个进行接触并确定他们提出停战条件的人。

sentences.en: And they were actually willing to talk about terms this time and they weren't going to be rejected out of hand.
sentences.zh: 他们这次其实愿意谈论条件，而且不会被断然拒绝。

sentences.en: And it then went up the chain of command and it got to general level where the chief of staff of the 64th Army,
sentences.zh: 然后它逐级上报，到达了将领级别，第64集团军参谋长，

sentences.en: which had been defending the south of the city, he was sent in, a guy called Lashkin.
sentences.zh: 该集团军一直防守该市南部，他被派了进去，一个叫拉什金（Lashkin）的人。

sentences.en: He was in there and he was the one who then sat down with Paulus and him and his officers were visibly shocked by the state of Paulus.
sentences.zh: 他在里面，他是那个坐下来与保卢斯会面的人，他和他的军官们对保卢斯的状态感到震惊。

sentences.en: Emaciated, gaunt, slightly unshaven, uniform slightly a bit of a mess, not really the wherewithal to really understand what was being said.
sentences.zh: 骨瘦如柴，憔悴，略带胡茬，制服有点一团糟，没有真正理解所说的话的能力。

sentences.en: But again, when you read the unpublished memoir of Rosker, it was actually Rosker who was in charge of the first communications.
sentences.zh: 但同样，当你阅读罗斯科未出版的回忆录时，实际上是罗斯科负责了第一次通讯。

sentences.en: He'd gone out and knocked on a tank and said, we want to now discuss surrender terms, send your party over.
sentences.zh: 他走出去敲了一辆坦克，说，我们现在想讨论投降条件，派你们的人过来吧。

sentences.en: And that was the first connection made to the enemy that was only a few hundred yards away from them.
sentences.zh: 那是与距离他们只有几百码远的敌人的第一次联系。

sentences.en: And obviously they're surrounded by artillery tanks and heavily armoured infantry.
sentences.zh: 显然他们被大炮、坦克和重装甲步兵包围了。

sentences.en: They have no chance.
sentences.zh: 他们毫无胜算。

sentences.en: They're barely holding on.
sentences.zh: 他们已经苦苦支撑。

sentences.en: But before even Paulus had turned up, it was Rosker who'd announced to the Russian leadership, we have the field marshal in the building.
sentences.zh: 但甚至在保卢斯出现之前，罗斯克就向苏联领导层宣布了：我们把元帅带进大楼了。

sentences.en: Up until then, they had no idea where Paulus was.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他们根本不知道保卢斯在哪里。

sentences.en: And therefore it was Rosker who kind of choreographed what was going on over the next few hours and how the Russians would deal with their surrender.
sentences.zh: 因此，可以说是罗斯克策划了接下来的几个小时里发生的一切，以及苏联人将如何处理他们的投降。

sentences.en: As in, no one's going to be shocked.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，没有人会感到震惊。

sentences.en: Officers to a level can keep some side arMs.
sentences.zh: 军官在一定级别上可以保留一些随身武器。

sentences.en: They're going to be supplied with food.
sentences.zh: 他们将获得食物供应。

sentences.en: Their sick will be treated fairly.
sentences.zh: 他们的伤员将得到公正对待。

sentences.en: Whether that happened or not, I'm sure it did.
sentences.zh: 不管这有没有发生，我相信是有的。

sentences.en: Lots of instances, I'm sure it didn't.
sentences.zh: 有很多情况，我确信没有。

sentences.en: Well, all the SS get shot, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所有的党卫军都被枪决了，不是吗？

sentences.en: And any Russians who were in German uniform to get shot?
sentences.zh: 任何穿德军制服的苏联人也都被枪决了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I was going to say the hardcore, there was a hardcore that still fought on for a few weeks after the surrender in the northern sector.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我本来想说的是核心分子，在北部战区投降后的几个星期里，仍然有一支核心力量在继续战斗。

sentences.en: And it took over, I think it was something like 10,000 security troops had to go into the city, the ruins of the city, once Paulus's surrender had been official,
sentences.zh: 据我估计，大概有一万名安全部队不得不进入这座城市，进入这片废墟，一旦保卢斯的投降正式化，

sentences.en: to flush out this final nest of survivors who were just not going to give in.
sentences.zh: 去清剿这最后的一群绝不妥协的幸存者。

sentences.en: And maybe some of them were SS.
sentences.zh: 也许其中一些人是党卫军。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: The official records don't say that.
sentences.zh: 官方记录并没有这么说。

sentences.en: But they were going to go down fighting.
sentences.zh: 但他们是要战至最后一兵一卒的。

sentences.en: And I think out of the thousands, I think it was 8,000 to 9,000 were there that had to be flushed out.
sentences.zh: 我想在那几千人中，大概有八千到九千人需要在那里被清剿。

sentences.en: And only 2,000 were captured.
sentences.zh: 而只有两千人被俘。

sentences.en: But in your book, you say that the prisoners, the SS prisoners and the Russians who've been in German uniform, they just get shot straight off.
sentences.zh: 但在你的书中，你说俘虏，党卫军俘虏和穿过德军制服的苏联人，他们直接就被枪决了。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: I mean, there was a lot of that going on wholesale, if not the back of a building or just taking away.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种大规模枪决的事情有很多，哪怕不是在建筑物后面，就是被带走处决。

sentences.en: There's one point that I capture about, which I hadn't read before,
sentences.zh: 我记录下的其中一点，是我以前没读过的，

sentences.en: where as Paulus is being put into a staff car to take him to 64th Army headquarters to be the famous filming of him,
sentences.zh: 当保卢斯被塞进一辆参谋车，被带去第六十四集团军总部进行那次著名的拍摄时，

sentences.en: one Russian recognises him and marches up to him with a machine gun and just wanted to take him out then and there.
sentences.zh: 一个苏联人认出了他，端着机枪气势汹汹地走过去，当时就想把他解决掉。

sentences.en: And he had to be restrained.
sentences.zh: 而他被人拦住了。

sentences.en: And Paulus is visibly shocked by this.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯对此感到明显震惊。

sentences.en: So Paulus, he gets taken to Moscow, is that right?
sentences.zh: 所以保卢斯被带到了莫斯科，是这样吗？

sentences.en: And he basically flips.
sentences.zh: 他基本上彻底倒戈了。

sentences.en: He becomes a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 他成了一个共产主义者。

sentences.en: Well, they were taken.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们被带走了。

sentences.en: The majority of the 90 or 1,000 that surrendered were marched into captivity, but, you know, march of death for many of them for the disease and the cold and the lack of...
sentences.zh: 投降的那九万或十万人中，大多数都被押送进战俘营，但你知道，对许多人来说，由于疾病、严寒和缺乏物资，这是一场死亡行军……

sentences.en: Because, again, they weren't expected to capture so many prisoners, they didn't have the supplies to feed them.
sentences.zh: 因为同样地，他们没有料到会俘虏这么多人，他们没有足够的物资来养活他们。

sentences.en: They could barely feed their own troops.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至快养不活自己的军队了。

sentences.en: So there was a huge casualty rate and drop-off of prisoners within weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 所以在几周和几个月内，战俘的伤亡率和减员率极高。

sentences.en: But, yeah, the elite of the German command were taken to special camps.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，德国指挥层的精锐被带到了特殊营地。

sentences.en: And it was there over the coming months and duration of the war that, yeah,
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，在接下来的几个月和战争的持续期间，是的，

sentences.en: quite a few of them did flip to the other side and they realised that fighting for National Socialism wasn't what it should be and calling upon their comrades to do the right thing.
sentences.zh: 他们中有相当多的人确实倒戈了，他们意识到为国家社会主义战斗并不是那么回事，并呼吁他们的同志做正确的事。

sentences.en: And Paulus was taken to the Nuremberg Trials.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯被带到了纽伦堡审判。

sentences.en: He's one of the witnesses.
sentences.zh: 他是证人之一。

sentences.en: And he ends up living in East Germany, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他最后住在东德，对吗？

sentences.en: He does, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的确住在那里。

sentences.en: And Roscoe, you talked about, who's one of the central characters, really, in your book.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了罗斯科，他确实是你书中的核心人物之一。

sentences.en: So he actually stays in it.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实一直待在那里。

sentences.en: He's in prison for more than 10 years, until 1955.
sentences.zh: 他在监狱里关了十多年，直到1955年。

sentences.en: So one of the last people to be released, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想他是最后一批被释放的人之一。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He was tried.
sentences.zh: 他受审了。

sentences.en: Look at his prison records.
sentences.zh: 看看他的监狱档案。

sentences.en: He was tried as a war criminal.
sentences.zh: 他作为战犯受审。

sentences.en: But many of them were, many of the senior officers were, and he, yeah, he did about 12 years, the early part of which, first two or three years, was hard labour.
sentences.zh: 但他们中的许多人，许多高级军官都是如此，而他，是的，他服刑了大约12年，其中早期，也就是前两三年，是苦役。

sentences.en: He moved around the prison of war archipelago.
sentences.zh: 他在战俘群岛各地辗转。

sentences.en: So he was in Siberia.
sentences.zh: 所以他在西伯利亚。

sentences.en: He was in the Urals.
sentences.zh: 他在乌拉尔。

sentences.en: He was down by the Black Sea.
sentences.zh: 他在黑海边。

sentences.en: And he was in Stalingrad because they used quite a lot of POW, German POWs, to rebuild Stalingrad over the next few years.
sentences.zh: 他还在斯大林格勒，因为在接下来的几年里，他们使用了相当多的德国战俘来重建斯大林格勒。

sentences.en: So he came home in the last year of the last transports, coming back from the east to West Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以他在最后一批从东方运回西德的运输船上回到了家。

sentences.en: And he came home to Dusseldorf in the summer of 1955.
sentences.zh: 他在1955年夏天回到了杜塞尔多夫。

sentences.en: I mean, he met his youngest son he'd never seen before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他见到了他从未见过的小儿子。

sentences.en: And that's one of the things I capture.
sentences.zh: 这也是我记录的事情之一。

sentences.en: Paulus tells him in the ruins of the Univamag, while they're getting bombed, news has just come through on the radio that your wife's had a son.
sentences.zh: 保卢斯在尤玛马克百货公司的废墟中告诉他，正当他们遭到轰炸时，收音机里刚传来消息，你妻子生了个儿子。

sentences.en: And he has to go off into an antechamber to cry because he's, obviously, it's emotional news.
sentences.zh: 他不得不走到一个小房间里去哭泣，因为很显然，这是一个充满情感的消息。

sentences.en: But, yeah, so he meets this son for the first time.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，所以他第一次见到了这个儿子。

sentences.en: But whatever was going on in his head, whether it's PTSD or guilt, or he just couldn't, after everything he'd been through, he couldn't settle down.
sentences.zh: 但不管他脑子里在想什么，无论是创伤后应激障碍、负罪感，还是在经历了这一切之后，他就是无法安定下来。

sentences.en: He sadly committed suicide, Christmas Day, 1956.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他在1956年的圣诞节自杀了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's incredible when you think 1956, you know, the year that Bill Haley and the Comets are touring Britain, you know, rock and roll, all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你想到1956年时，这太不可思议了，你知道，那是比尔·海利与彗星乐队在英国巡演的年份，你知道，摇滚乐，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: That the war is still sufficiently fresh in people's minds and that the scars of it are still so raw that people are coming home and, you know,
sentences.zh: 战争在人们的记忆中依然如此新鲜，战争的伤疤依然如此历历在目，以至于人们回到家后，你知道，

sentences.en: taking their own lives because of the traumas they've suffered.
sentences.zh: 因为他们遭受的创伤而结束了自己的生命。

sentences.en: But talking of the freshness of the memories of Stalingrad, obviously, for the Soviet Union, and then when the Soviet Union falls, Russia as well, Stalingrad is the great victory,
sentences.zh: 但说到斯大林格勒记忆的新鲜感，显然，对于苏联，后来当苏联解体时，对于俄罗斯来说，斯大林格勒是伟大的胜利，

sentences.en: isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: It's the great crowning victory.
sentences.zh: 这是最伟大的加冕胜利。

sentences.en: Yeah, especially today.
sentences.zh: 是的，尤其是今天。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the one thing I, you couldn't ignore it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我的一点感受，你无法忽视它。

sentences.en: When I was on my trip, I met several historians there, had dinner with them.
sentences.zh: 当我在那里旅行时，我在那里遇到了几位历史学家，和他们共进晚餐。

sentences.en: We had a really good chat and discussed lots of aspects of the story itself that I'm talking about and of Stalingrad as a whole.
sentences.zh: 我们聊得很开心，讨论了我正在谈论的故事本身的许多方面，以及斯大林格勒作为一个整体的方方面面。

sentences.en: And to them, yes.
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, even if you park Putin to one side and whatever agenda he's setting right now, and he has set over the last couple of decades, to them,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使你把普京放在一边，不管他现在制定了什么议程，以及他在过去几十年里制定了什么议程，对他们而言，

sentences.en: Stalingrad is the cornerstone of what happened in the Great Patriotic War.
sentences.zh: 斯大林格勒是卫国战争中发生的一切的基石。

sentences.en: And along with other cities, I mean, there's over 10 of them,
sentences.zh: 与其他城市一样，我的意思是，有十多个城市，

sentences.en: but Stalingrad was one of the first cities to be called a hero city or designated a hero city by Stalin to be celebrated as such.
sentences.zh: 但斯大林格勒是第一批被称为英雄城市或被斯大林指定为英雄城市并作为英雄城市来庆祝的城市之一。

sentences.en: And ironically, Kiev is one of them too.
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，基辅也是其中之一。

sentences.en: And Odessa is as well.
sentences.zh: 敖德萨也是。

sentences.en: And so to Russians, it really, I mean, I can't overemphasize how much it means to them.
sentences.zh: 所以对于俄罗斯人来说，这真的，我的意思是，我怎么强调它对他们的意义都不为过。

sentences.en: When I was there, I was standing outside Pavlov's house on a freezing cold day.
sentences.zh: 当我在那里时，我在一个寒冷刺骨的日子里站在巴甫洛夫的房子外面。

sentences.en: It was about minus 10, minus 12, probably minus 20 in the chill, taking photos of the house.
sentences.zh: 气温大约是零下10度、零下12度，算上风寒效应可能达到零下20度，我正在给那栋房子拍照。

sentences.en: And I got there really early in the morning thinking no one will be here.
sentences.zh: 我一大早就到了那里，以为不会有人在那里。

sentences.en: It was about nine o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那时大约早上九点。

sentences.en: There was about 200, 300 of them standing behind me that were doing the tour, going along the Volga, taking the photos of Pavlov's house.
sentences.zh: 我身后站着大约两三百人，他们正在进行旅游团活动，沿着伏尔加河走，拍摄巴甫洛夫的房子的照片。

sentences.en: And as you say, Dominic, I know it's in a call of duty, but there's other things.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，多米尼克，我知道这在《使命召唤》里出现过，但还有别的东西。

sentences.en: Children are educated about it constantly.
sentences.zh: 孩子们不断地接受关于它的教育。

sentences.en: It's constantly at the front of Russian military history, Russian history of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 它始终处于俄罗斯军事史、20世纪俄罗斯历史的最前沿。

sentences.en: And yet, is there an irony here?
sentences.zh: 然而，这里面是否包含着一种讽刺？

sentences.en: Well, there are loads of ironies, but is one irony, Ian, that, I mean, you actually agree with James Holland in our Barbarossa podcast,
sentences.zh: 嗯，讽刺的地方有很多，但其中一个讽刺是，伊恩，我的意思是，你实际上同意我们在《巴巴罗萨》播客中詹姆斯·霍兰的看法，

sentences.en: that the German drive, you know, eastwards and south was doomed anyway.
sentences.zh: 即德军向东和向南的推进无论如何都是注定要失败的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I just, especially after the first year, I can't understand why they thought they could conquer so much land.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我只是，特别是在第一年之后，我无法理解他们怎么会认为自己能征服那么多的土地。

sentences.en: That's the thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: But having launched it, what else could they do?
sentences.zh: 但既然已经发动了进攻，他们还能做什么呢？

sentences.en: No, I agree.
sentences.zh: 不，我同意。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, I mean, it's Hobson's choice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，这就是霍布森的选择（无可选择的选择）。

sentences.en: It wasn't like they could say, oh, sorry, we've made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他们可以说，哦，对不起，我们搞错了。

sentences.en: Let's patch things up.
sentences.zh: 让我们重修旧好吧。

sentences.en: But equally compounded by the fact that he declares war on America.
sentences.zh: 但这同样因他向美国宣战的事实而雪上加霜。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, Hitler's hopeless, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 对，好吧，希特勒无可救药，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, but he's instigated his own downfall before they even launched Case Blue.
sentences.zh: 对，对，但在他们甚至还没发起“蓝色行动”之前，他就已经促成了自己的垮台。

sentences.en: And he's seen that from a strategic point of view, whereas the troops on the ground, you read the letters, you read the diaries, they did feel like this was it.
sentences.zh: 从战略角度来看，这一点他已经看出来了，而地面部队，你读信件，你读日记，他们确实觉得这就是一切。

sentences.en: This was their crusade.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的十字军东征。

sentences.en: The communique Roska gives to his company commanders, because he led his regiment to capture the river right at the start of the battle.
sentences.zh: 罗斯科发给他连长的电报，因为他在战役刚开始时就率领他的团攻占了河流。

sentences.en: He's the first Germans on the river in the city.
sentences.zh: 他是城里第一批抵达河边的德国人。

sentences.en: He gave a communique to his troops, declaring that we do this.
sentences.zh: 他向他的部队发了一封电报，宣布我们做到了。

sentences.en: The war's almost won.
sentences.zh: 战争快要赢了。

sentences.en: We get to the river.
sentences.zh: 我们到了河边。

sentences.en: It's done.
sentences.zh: 这就结束了。

sentences.en: And you just think, what were they thinking?
sentences.zh: 你就会想，他们在想什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, Ian, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 好的，伊恩，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Tour de Force and your new book, The Lighthouse of Stalingrad, The Hidden Truth, the centre of World War II's greatest battle, is out now?
sentences.zh: 这是一部杰作，你的新书《斯大林格勒灯塔：二战最伟大战役中心的隐藏真相》现在已经出版了吗？

sentences.en: Comes out 28th of July.
sentences.zh: 7月28日出版。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So that's The Lighthouse of Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 这就是《斯大林格勒灯塔》。

sentences.en: I can't recommend it enough.
sentences.zh: 我极力推荐这本书。

sentences.en: It is immensely readable, but it is a very harrowing story.
sentences.zh: 它非常具有可读性，但这是一个非常让人心碎的故事。

sentences.en: But, Tom, I don't know if you agree, but harrowing stories are often the best, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，我不知道你是否同意，但让人心碎的故事往往是最好的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's definitely harrowing.
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是让人心碎的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I've never actually – so I haven't read Anthony Beaver's book.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我其实从来没有——所以我没有读过安东尼·比弗的书。

sentences.en: It's a terrible thing to admit.
sentences.zh: 承认这一点是一件很糟糕的事。

sentences.en: I haven't seen the Jude Law film.
sentences.zh: 我没看过裘德·洛演的那部电影。

sentences.en: I haven't played Call of Duty in the house.
sentences.zh: 我家里也没玩过《使命召唤》。

sentences.en: So I really – the depths of my ignorance about The Battle of Stalingrad are enormous.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的——我对斯大林格勒战役的无知程度是巨大的。

sentences.en: But Ian's –
sentences.zh: 但伊恩的——

sentences.en: Yeah, it's shocking.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I can't believe you have the effrontery to appear on a history podcast after those admissions.
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信你在承认了这些之后，还有脸出现在历史播客节目中。

sentences.en: Well, but now I've read Ian's book and I know all about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但现在我读了伊恩的书，我对一切都了如指掌了。

sentences.en: I meant to say one thing I forgot to say, which I think is really key, actually.
sentences.zh: 我本来想说一件事，但我忘了说，我认为这其实真的很关键。

sentences.en: And whether they still go ahead with it, I'd be super surprised because of what's going on right now.
sentences.zh: 鉴于目前正在发生的事情，如果他们仍然继续推进这件事，我会感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: So the historians that I had dinner with in Volgograd were launching a campaign to change the name of Pavlov's house.
sentences.zh: 所以我在伏尔加格勒共进晚餐的历史学家们正在发起一场运动，要改变巴甫洛夫的房子的名字。

sentences.en: Oh, I thought you were going to say Volgograd back to Stalingrad.
sentences.zh: 哦，我还以为你要说把伏尔加格勒改回斯大林格勒呢。

sentences.en: Well, no, but they are allowed to call it Stalingrad six times a year to do with various dates in the diary to do with the war.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有，但他们一年中可以有六次称它为斯大林格勒，这与日历上与战争有关的各种日期有关。

sentences.en: But they wanted to change the name of Pavlov's house to Afanasayev's house because they feel that's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 但他们想把巴甫洛夫的房子改名为阿法纳西耶夫的房子，因为他们觉得那是正确的事情。

sentences.en: So whether they disappear from view now, who knows?
sentences.zh: 所以它们现在是否会从人们的视野中消失，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Maybe call it Afanasayev and Pavlov's house.
sentences.zh: 也许叫阿法纳西耶夫和巴甫洛夫的房子吧。

sentences.en: Or is that too wordy?
sentences.zh: 或者那样名字太长了？

sentences.en: That's the Liberal Democrat solution there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 那是自由民主党的解决方案，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's very, very Liberal Democrat.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常符合自由民主党的风格。

sentences.en: Anyway, thanks never so much.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，非常感谢。

sentences.en: I think we have put the battle of Stalingrad to bed.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经把斯大林格勒战役尘埃落定了。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: And thank you to Ian for coming on.
sentences.zh: 感谢伊恩作客节目。

sentences.en: And we will see you soon for more history-based, well, fun isn't the word, stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会带来更多以历史为基础的……好吧，说“好玩”不太合适，总之是这方面的内容。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thanks for listening to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史的剩余》。

sentences.zh: 如需收听加更节目、提前畅听、免广告收听并加入我们的聊天社群，请登录 restishistorypod.com 注册。
